notes:
Follow-up release fixing two visible-in-the-OS-shell brand bugs that stayed wrong after v1.0.33: the green folded-S icon was sitting inside a charcoal rounded square in every Windows surface (taskbar, alt-tab, file-explorer, jump lists, system tray), and the dashboard sidebar wordmark was rendering as styled text with the system font drawing letterforms that don't match the actual brand. No functional changes for the trading engine. This is a normal point release - both v1.0.33 and v1.0.34 share the `com.asasystems.terminal` Tauri identifier, so v1.0.33 users update via the in-app updater the same way every other point release lands. No manual install required. ### Fixes - **App / taskbar / tray icon backgrounds are now transparent.** v1.0.30→v1.0.33 composited every icon sub-image (16/24/32/48/64/128/256 inside `tray-app/src-tauri/icons/icon.ico` and the standalone `32x32.png` / `64x64.png` / `128x128.png` / `128x128@2x.png` / `icon.png` Tauri reads from `bundle.icon[]`) onto a charcoal `#0E1011` rounded square. That meant every Windows surface that paints its own background (taskbar, alt-tab, file-explorer thumbnail, Start-menu jump list, system tray) showed a green-S-on-charcoal-square sitting on top of the system-painted background — visually a black tile around the brand mark. Brave, Discord, Telegram, and every other modern Windows app render their icons as glyph-on-transparent so the system shell paints the surrounding chrome. `scripts/build_icon.py` now drops `rounded_square()` entirely, composites the green folded-S directly onto an all-alpha-zero canvas at ~92 % glyph fill, and writes a multi-frame .ico where every sub-image is RGBA with transparent corners. The change propagated to all four .ico mirrors (`tray-app/src-tauri/icons/icon.ico`, `branding/png/icon.ico`, `build/asa-terminal.ico` for the PyInstaller `server.exe` icon, `marketing/landing/branding/icon.ico` for the landing favicon) plus all five Tauri standalone PNGs and all five landing PNGs (`favicon-{16,32,48,64}.png`, `apple-touch-icon-180.png`). Verified all 26 surfaces have alpha=0 corners and 19-25 % fill ratio (down from ~95 % on the v1.0.33 charcoal-square versions). - **App icon is now sharp at every size, not just legible.** The same charcoal-square fix doubles as a sharpness fix. Inside the v1.0.33 32×32 frame, the green folded-S only got ~22×22 pixels worth of detail because the rounded-square margin ate ~30 % of the canvas. When Windows downscaled to ~24×24 for the taskbar at 100 % DPI, the S detail squashed to ~16×16 visible — soft and indistinct. v1.0.34 fills ~92 % of every frame with the S itself, so the same 24×24 taskbar render now has ~22 px of real S detail. The user reported "the wizard icon is high quality but the dashboard icon on the taskbar isn't high quality" against v1.0.33 — same icon source, but the wizard renders at NSIS dialog size (32-48 px) where the v1.0.33 charcoal-margin penalty was small, while the taskbar renders at exactly the size the margin hurt most. Switching to glyph-on-transparent at 92 % fill resolves both surfaces simultaneously. - **ICO file structure switched to BMP-for-≤128 + PNG-for-256.** Pillow's default `Image.save(format='ICO')` produced PNG-encoded sub-images for every frame, including the small ones. Some Windows shell paths still prefer BMP-encoded sub-images at sizes ≤128 (the convention `shell32.dll` itself uses) and PNG only at 256 (where BMP at 32-bit RGBA is ~256 KB per frame). `scripts/build_icon.py` now writes the .ico container manually via `struct` so the encoding mix matches the convention exactly: BITMAPINFOHEADER with doubled height + bottom-up BGRA + AND mask for ≤128, raw PNG bytes for 256. Eliminates the encoding ambiguity that may have been a contributing factor to the icon-quality mismatch between Tauri-embedded (winres) and NSIS-`installerIcon` consumers of the same icon.ico file. - **Dashboard sidebar wordmark is now the actual Copilot brand mark, not styled text.** `dashboard.html:33` rendered the persistent left-rail wordmark as a chart-line SVG icon plus `ASA Terminal`. The chart icon was decorative and unrelated to the brand. The "ASA" text was just whatever the system font drew at 18 px — the real brand mark in `branding/png/wordmark-master.png` has chevron A's *without crossbars* and a geometric folded S, neither of which any text font produces. Replaced both: the chart SVG is gone, and the styled-text "ASA" span is replaced with `` followed by a green "Terminal" word. The image is a 560×198 raster cropped from `wordmark-master.png` by `scripts/build_icon.py` (uses a non-dark-pixel bbox so all three glyphs — chevron-A, folded-S, chevron-A — are captured; the green-only key from earlier passes was clipping the white A's). CSS in `static/css/components.css` height-locks the image at 24 px so it sits flush with the 18 px "Terminal" text. - **Login, onboarding, and admin headings show the real wordmark too.** Same root cause as the dashboard sidebar — `templates/login.html:88`, `templates/onboarding.html:58`, and `templates/admin.html:63` all rendered `

ASA Terminal

` as styled text. v1.0.34 swaps the leading `ASA ` for `` in all three, with per-template CSS rules (`.logo .wordmark-asa` for login, `.wordmark-asa` for onboarding, `.header h1 .wordmark-asa` for admin) sizing the image at 26-30 px so it pairs with the existing h1 type. The "Terminal" word stays as styled text because "Terminal" is just a plain English word and was never part of the brand mark — only "ASA" needs the raster. - **Tray-app splash wordmark uses the bundled raster too.** `tray-app/src/App.tsx` rendered the splash heading as `

ASA Terminal

` styled text. v1.0.34 imports `wordmark-header.png` as a Vite asset (`import wordmarkUrl from "./assets/wordmark-header.png"`) so Vite emits a hashed asset URL into the build output. The splash has to render before the Flask sidecar boots, so it can't fetch the image from `/static/...` — bundling it is the only option. `scripts/build_icon.py` writes the same 560×198 raster to `tray-app/src/assets/wordmark-header.png` on every icon rebuild so the tray-app and Flask copies stay in sync. v1.0.32 → v1.0.33 → v1.0.34 sequence on this surface: hand-coded SVG paths (wrong geometry) → styled text (right characters but wrong letterforms) → actual brand raster (right). ### Tauri vs NSIS icon embedding investigated User reported that v1.0.33's NSIS installer wizard icon looked sharp while the running app's taskbar icon looked blurry — implying Tauri's compile-time icon embedding was using a different (lower-quality) source than NSIS's `installerIcon` config. Investigation: `tray-app/src-tauri/build.rs` is just `tauri_build::build()` (no winres override), `Cargo.toml` has no `[package.metadata.winres]` section, and `tauri.conf.json` declares `bundle.icon = ["icons/32x32.png", "icons/64x64.png", "icons/128x128.png", "icons/128x128@2x.png", "icons/icon.ico"]` plus `bundle.windows.nsis.installerIcon = "icons/icon.ico"`. tauri-build picks the .ico from `bundle.icon[]` and embeds all of its sub-images via winres into the resulting `asa-terminal.exe`; NSIS reads the same .ico. So they ARE coming from the same source — meaning the visual mismatch was about *what was inside that .ico*: charcoal-square frames that look fine at NSIS dialog sizes but blur at taskbar size. The transparent-bg + 92 %-fill regeneration above fixes it for both consumers simultaneously. ### Auto-updater note Same shipping pipeline as v1.0.30 → v1.0.33: PyInstaller `server.exe` sidecar -> Tauri NSIS bundle -> manual minisign with `npx tauri signer sign -f - -p ""` from bash (NOT auto-signer in PowerShell pipes — that produces 0-byte sigs) -> SHA256 + UTF-8-no-BOM `latest.json` -> `gh release create` -> uploaded to `cjml34483/TradeSpace-releases`. v1.0.33 -> v1.0.34 auto-updates cleanly because the Tauri identifier hasn't changed.
